name: Prudential Financial
description: Prudential Financial is a life insurer, retirement-plan and annuity provider, and global asset manager. Its largest earnings pools are retirement and pension-risk transfer products in the U.S. and life insurance sold in Japan, Brazil and other markets through its own Life Planner sales force (PRU, Prudential of Japan and Gibraltar Life). It also runs PGIM, an investment manager with about $1.466 trillion under management that earns percentage-of-assets fees, and group life and disability cover for employers. Profit comes from the spread between investment income and what it credits to policyholders, underwriting margins on premiums, and asset-management fees. In February 2026 it voluntarily suspended new sales at Prudential of Japan for 90 days after an internal investigation into employee misconduct.

sub.name: Life, retirement and supplemental health insurers

employees.note: 13,879 in the U.S. and 22,945 outside the U.S. (36,607 full-time equivalents); excludes independent contractors. Separately, 13,218 Life Planners and Life Consultants sell its International products.

businessLines.name: International Businesses (Japan, Brazil and others)
businessLines.how: Policyholders pay recurring premiums for life, accident and health and retirement products sold mainly by its own Life Planners and Life Consultants and through banks and agencies in Japan and other markets; it earns underwriting margin plus investment spread. Annualized new business premiums were $2,205M in 2025.

businessLines.name: Retirement Strategies: Institutional Retirement Strategies
businessLines.how: Pension plan sponsors and insurers pay a single premium to transfer pension obligations (pension-risk transfer) or fund long-term retirement and structured-settlement liabilities; Prudential earns the spread between investment income and benefits it pays out.

businessLines.name: Retirement Strategies: Individual Retirement Strategies
businessLines.how: Individuals buy variable, fixed-indexed and registered-index-linked annuities, often through advisors; Prudential earns fees on account values plus investment spread, with guarantees it must hedge.

businessLines.name: Group Insurance
businessLines.how: Employers and associations pay premiums for group life, disability and accidental death cover, renewed annually, and Prudential earns the underwriting margin. Premiums mostly come from the National Market (employers with more than 5,000 benefit-eligible employees).
